records.title: Continuous image of a compact space
records.statement:
Assume $X,Y$ are topological spaces; $X$ is compact. $f:X\to Y$ is continuous.

Then The image $f(X)$ is compact.

records.title: Closed subspace of a compact space
records.statement:
Assume $X$ is a compact topological space. $F\subseteq X$ is closed.

Then The subspace $F$ is compact.

records.title: Continuous image of a connected space
records.statement:
Assume $X,Y$ are topological spaces. $A\subseteq X$ is connected. $f:X\to Y$ is continuous.

Then $f(A)$ is connected.

records.title: Heine–Cantor theorem
records.statement:
Assume $X$ is a compact metric space. $Y$ is a metric space. $f:X\to Y$ is continuous.

Then $f$ is uniformly continuous.

records.title: Heine–Borel theorem
hypotheses: $K$ is a subset of Euclidean space $\mathbb R^n$, with $n\ge1$.
conclusions: $K$ is compact if and only if $K$ is closed and bounded.

records.title: Intermediate value theorem
conclusions: There exists $c\in[a,b]$ with $f(c)=u$ (and $c\in(a,b)$ if $u$ lies strictly between the endpoint values).
records.statement:
Assume $f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is continuous. $u$ lies between $f(a)$ and $f(b)$.

Then There exists $c\in[a,b]$ with $f(c)=u$ (and $c\in(a,b)$ if $u$ lies strictly between the endpoint values).

records.title: Extreme value theorem
hypotheses: $K$ is a nonempty compact metric space.
conclusions: There exist $x_{\min},x_{\max}\in K$ with $f(x_{\min})\le f(x)\le f(x_{\max})$ for every $x\in K$.
records.statement:
Assume $K$ is a nonempty compact metric space. $f:K\to\mathbb R$ is continuous.

Then There exist $x_{\min},x_{\max}\in K$ with $f(x_{\min})\le f(x)\le f(x_{\max})$ for every $x\in K$.

records.title: Rolle's theorem
hypotheses: $a<b$; $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$.
records.statement:
Assume $a<b$; $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$. $f(a)=f(b)$.

Then There exists $c\in(a,b)$ such that $f'(c)=0$.

records.title: Mean value theorem
hypotheses: $a<b$; $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$.
records.statement:
Assume $a<b$; $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$.

Then For some $c\in(a,b)$, $f'(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$.

records.title: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem
hypotheses: $(x_n)$ is a bounded sequence of real numbers.
records.statement:
Assume $(x_n)$ is a bounded sequence of real numbers.

Then There is a convergent subsequence $(x_{n_k})$.

records.title: Banach fixed-point theorem
hypotheses: $(X,d)$ is a nonempty complete metric space.
$f:X\to X$ is a contraction: for some $0\le q<1$, $d(f(x),f(y))\le qd(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in X$.
conclusions: $f$ has exactly one fixed point. Iteration of $f$ from any starting point converges to it.
records.statement:
Assume $(X,d)$ is a nonempty complete metric space. $f:X\to X$ is a contraction: for some $0\le q<1$, $d(f(x),f(y))\le qd(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in X$.

Then $f$ has exactly one fixed point. Iteration of $f$ from any starting point converges to it.

records.title: Rank–nullity theorem
hypotheses: $V$ is a finite-dimensional vector space and $W$ a vector space over the same field.
records.statement:
Assume $V$ is a finite-dimensional vector space and $W$ a vector space over the same field. $T:V\to W$ is linear.

Then $\dim(\ker T)+\dim(\operatorname{im}T)=\dim V$.

records.title: Lagrange's theorem (groups)
records.statement:
Assume $G$ is a finite group. $H\le G$ is a subgroup.

Then $|H|$ divides $|G|$, and $[G:H]=|G|/|H|$.

records.title: Orbit–stabilizer theorem
hypotheses: A finite group $G$ acts on a finite set $X$.
records.statement:
Assume A finite group $G$ acts on a finite set $X$. Fix $x\in X$.

Then $|\operatorname{Orb}_G(x)|=[G:\operatorname{Stab}_G(x)]=|G|/|\operatorname{Stab}_G(x)|$.

records.title: Fermat's little theorem
records.statement:
Assume $p$ is prime. $a$ is an integer and $p\nmid a$.

Then $a^{p-1}\equiv1\pmod p$.

records.title: Cantor's theorem
conclusions: There is no surjection $S\to\mathcal P(S)$; in particular $|S|<|\mathcal P(S)|$.
records.statement:
Assume $S$ is a set.

Then There is no surjection $S\to\mathcal P(S)$; in particular $|S|<|\mathcal P(S)|$.

records.title: Bayes' theorem
hypotheses: $A,B$ are events in a probability space with $P(A)>0$ and $P(B)>0$.
records.statement:
Assume $A,B$ are events in a probability space with $P(A)>0$ and $P(B)>0$.

Then $P(B\mid A)=\frac{P(A\mid B)P(B)}{P(A)}$.

hypotheses: $n$ distinct objects are partitioned among $k$ classes with integers $0<k<n$.
conclusions: Some class contains at least two objects.

records.title: Cauchy's inequality (real sequences)
records.statement:
Assume $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ and $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ are finite real sequences.

Then $\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n r_i s_i\bigr)^2\le\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n r_i^2\bigr)\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n s_i^2\bigr)$.

records.title: Triangle inequality for real numbers
records.statement:
Assume $x,y$ are real numbers.

Then $|x+y|\le|x|+|y|$.
